comparisons.peer_topic: USPB Expense and Credit Loss Trends
comparisons.peer_summary: USPB expenses decreased 1% to $10 billion due to productivity savings and lower technology costs, while cost of credit increased to $8.6 billion (from $6.7 billion) primarily due to a 45% rise in net credit losses from maturing card vintages and macroeconomic pressures on lower FICO band customers, partially offset by a lower ACL build.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C reported increased cost of credit driven by net credit losses in their consumer card portfolios. BAC specifically cited 'credit card loans' as a primary driver of the increased net charge-off ratio. C provided more granular detail, attributing a 45% rise in net credit losses to the maturation of card vintages and macroeconomic pressures (inflation, rates) impacting lower FICO band customers, which aligns with BAC’s mention of economic uncertainty impacting credit quality.

sentences.text: During 2024, our net charge-off ratio increased primarily driven by credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio.

Uncertainty remains regarding broader economic impacts due to higher costs associated with inflationary pressures experienced over the past several years, elevated rates as well as the current geopolitical environment, and could lead to adverse impacts to credit quality metrics in future periods.
Cost of credit increased to $8.6 billion, compared to $6.7 billion in the prior year.

The increase was driven by higher net credit losses (up 45%), primarily reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years, as well as macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment impacting both cards portfolios, with lower FICO band customers primarily driving the increase.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS reported an increase in credit loss provisions for 2024 driven primarily by net charge-offs in their respective credit card portfolios. However, while BAC also highlighted significant deterioration in the commercial real estate (CRE) office portfolio and broader commercial portfolios, GS’s 2024 provision increase was attributed almost exclusively to credit card net charge-offs, with no mention of CRE as a primary driver for the year-over-year increase.

sentences.text: During 2024, our net charge-off ratio increased primarily driven by credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio.
Nonperforming loans also increased compared to December 31, 2023 primarily driven by the U.S. commercial portfolio.
Provision for credit losses was $1.54 billion for 2024, compared with $1.14 billion for 2023.
Provisions for 2024 reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio (primarily driven by net charge-offs).

comparisons.peer_topic: Year-over-Year Provision for Credit Losses Analysis
comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.35 billion in 2024 from $1.03 billion in 2023. The 2024 increase was primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio, while 2023 provisions included credit card charge-offs and wholesale loan impairments, partially offset by reserve reductions related to the GreenSky and Marcus portfolio transactions.
comparisons.comparison: Similar to BAC, GS identified the credit card portfolio as the primary driver of increased credit losses in 2024. A key difference is that GS explicitly noted reserve reductions related to specific transactions (GreenSky and Marcus) in the prior year (2023) that inflated 2023 provisions, whereas BAC’s comparison focused on broad increases in criticized exposure and nonperforming loans without attributing prior year distortions to specific portfolio sales.

sentences.text: During 2024, our net charge-off ratio increased primarily driven by credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio.
Commercial reservable criticized exposure increased compared to December 31, 2023 driven by an increase across a broad range of industries.
Provision for credit losses in the consolidated statements of earnings was $1.35 billion for 2024, compared with $1.03 billion for 2023.

Provisions for 2023 reflected net provisions related to both the credit card portfolio (primarily driven by net charge-offs) and wholesale loans (primarily driven by impairments), partially offset by reserve reductions of $637 million related to the transfer of the GreenSky loan portfolio to held for sale and $442 million related to the sale of substantially all of the Marcus loan portfolio.

comparisons.peer_topic: Real Estate Exposure and Criticized Assets Changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Real Estate exposure was $207.1 billion as of December 31, 2024. Criticized exposure increased by $3.2 billion to $12.4 billion, driven by downgrades primarily in Multifamily and Office.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM reported increases in criticized exposure and nonperforming assets driven by the commercial real estate sector, specifically office properties. BAC noted that its 'commercial reservable criticized exposure' increased across a broad range of industries and that nonperforming loans rose primarily in the U.S. commercial portfolio. JPM similarly reported a $3.2 billion increase in criticized exposure driven by downgrades in Multifamily and Office, though JPM’s disclosure was specific to its Real Estate segment exposure rather than a broad commercial portfolio increase.

sentences.text: During 2024, our net charge-off ratio increased primarily driven by credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio.
Commercial reservable criticized exposure increased compared to December 31, 2023 driven by an increase across a broad range of industries.
Nonperforming loans also increased compared to December 31, 2023 primarily driven by the U.S. commercial portfolio.
Criticized exposure increased by $3.2 billion from $9.2 billion at December 31, 2023 to $12.4 billion at December 31, 2024, predominantly driven by downgrades, primarily in Multifamily and Office.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Provision for Credit Losses 2024 and 2023
comparisons.peer_summary: The provision for credit losses on loans and lending commitments was $62 million in 2024, driven by specific commercial real estate and securities-based loans and portfolio growth, and $131 million in 2023, driven by deteriorating conditions in the commercial real estate office sector.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS identified commercial real estate, specifically the office sector, as a significant driver of credit deterioration in 2024. BAC reported that the net charge-off ratio increased primarily driven by the 'commercial real estate office portfolio.' Similarly, MS noted that its 2023 provision was driven by deteriorating conditions in the commercial real estate sector, mainly office, and while its 2024 provision was lower, it was still related to specific commercial real estate loans. Both firms highlight the ongoing impact of the CRE office downturn on credit metrics.

sentences.text: During 2024, our net charge-off ratio increased primarily driven by credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio.

The Provision for credit losses on loans and lending commitments of $62 million in 2024 was primarily related to certain specific commercial real estate and securities-based loans, and portfolio growth, partially offset by improvements in the macroeconomic outlook.

The Provision for credit losses on loans and lending commitments of $131 million in 2023 was primarily related to deteriorating conditions in the commercial real estate sector including provisions for certain specific loans, mainly in the office portfolio.
